_comment: Units (DESIGN §3.2b, DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-07; every number here is DRAFT, ×3 scale — DESIGN §5.8). A unit carries people drawn from settlements (a proportional slice of every cohort; a levy takes men 15–44 only) and returns them when it settles or disbands. `enabled` says which types the player may raise in the current build: settlers in Phase 2 session 1; work-bands since session 2 (Session 16); levies since Session 19 (men 15–44, pay 1 coin a man a month, disband = a walk home, they garrison castles and may fortify). Costs: `money` from the faction treasury; materials from the raising settlement's cluster stockpile, the rest from the realm stockpile with a notice (instant — PLACEHOLDER until roads and caravans). `movePoints` per month against data/terrain.json moveCost (mountains take the whole month, lake and sea are impassable, a river hex is crossed only by a bridge or a settlement standing on it). `defaultSize`: a number of people, or "destination" = the hands the destination's seven hexes + hall + granary need, turned into people at the source's hands share. `defaultProvisions`: months, or "calendar" = months until the October harvest + 2 (max 12).

types.name: Settlers
types.blurb: Families with carts and seed grain, bound for new land. Founds a village where it stops; disbands only into an own settlement.

types.name: Work-band
types.blurb: Labourers who build roads and bridges (later quarries and castles); disbands only into an own settlement.

types.name: Levy
types.blurb: Men 15–44 called from a settlement; paid 1 coin a man a month and fed; they garrison castles, fortify the ground, and disband by walking home.

provisions._comment: months of food a unit may carry at most; the settlers' calendar default = months until harvestMonth (0 = January) + afterHarvestMonths. Inside own borders a unit refills to its chosen months from the cluster whose influence covers the hex.

foraging._comment: Outside the borders a unit works the food jobs of its hex and ring 1 with its own hands, best yield per hand first: fish and game at settlement efficiency, farming and herding at these shares of the hex's yield (Omer 2026-11-07), arriving monthly in twelfths (no harvest calendar — gleaning, not a harvest).

staffing._comment: Partial staffing of a food hex (DESIGN §3.2b rule 1, continuous reading confirmed by Omer 2026-11-07): at or above `full` the hex yields its staffing share; between `drop` and `full` each point below `full` costs `slope` points of output; below `drop` the hex is not worked and its hands try a smaller job before becoming spare. Buildings and material gathering stay linear.

muster._comment: a party may be gathered from the raising settlement, the other members of its cluster, and any own settlement within this many hexes; it forms on the raising settlement's hex at the next end of turn (the walk inside the cluster is abstracted — PLACEHOLDER until groups exist).

disband._comment: a unit disbands into the closest non-starving own settlement within this many hexes (the least starving if all are); none within reach → the order is refused.

settle._comment: settlers may found a village on any land hex except these terrains, outside every other settlement's work zone.

naming._comment: PLACEHOLDER until culture groups and naming exist (DESIGN §4.10): a new village is called after its home settlement.
